subject: BlueRidge private deployment — constraints, risks & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@blueridge-dx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueRidge private deployment — constraints, risks & next steps

Hi Daniel & Megan,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap while the items are fresh so we can align on the path forward. If anything below is inaccurate or needs clarification, flag it and I’ll update the doc.

Summary of primary goals you shared:
- Replace a portion of inference traffic for diagnostic image processing with a private/on-prem Redwood deployment to meet residency and regulatory controls.
- Maintain sub-200ms token latency for model-assisted triage workflows.
- Avoid any persistent egress of raw patient data off your network (audit requirement).

Key constraints you confirmed during the call:
1) Air-gapped / restricted egress posture: no outbound internet from the inference environment except to a whitelisted IP for licensing checks (rare, must be documented).
2) KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys (FIPS 140-2 or equivalent) required; HSM integration preferred.
3) Network: isolated VLAN with only specific CIDR ranges allowed for management and an ops bastion; no direct public IPs on model hosts.
4) Logging & audit: immutable audit logs must be retained 7+ years and accessible for audits; SOC2 evidence will be requested.
5) Procurement: PO + SOW with defined acceptance tests and a 30d pilot window.

Immediate asks / next steps we propose (owners):
- BlueRidge: share a high-level network diagram and list of allowed outbound endpoints/ports (Daniel) — due by EOD Friday (8/20).
- Redwood (Priyom + Ben): produce a secure deployment sketch and list of required firewall rules. Deliverable: "blueridge-network-sketch.pdf" — ETA Tue 8/24.
- Redwood (Marissa): draft SOW outline and pilot acceptance criteria and share for review — ETA Mon 8/23 (attached as redwood-sow-outline-v1.docx).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive for HSM/KMS integration with your security team (30–45m) — propose times below.

Proposed meeting slots for the technical deep-dive:
- Tue 8/24 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed 8/25 14:00–14:45 PT

Risks we raised on the call:
- If the environment cannot permit outbound checks for license validation, we may need an air-gapped licensing flow which adds ~2–3 weeks to onboarding.
- If the HSM environment is strictly offline and cannot accept PKI exchanges, some integrations will require custom work and SC signature transfers.

Attachments: redwood-sow-outline-v1.docx (SOW skeleton).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the network diagram and then Priyom/Ben will follow with the firewall/ops sketch.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform for predictable production serving

From: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@blueridge-dx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Li <megan.li@blueridge-dx.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueRidge private deployment — constraints, risks & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items and adding technical details from our infra/security teams below.

Confirmed constraints (short):
- No outbound to general internet from segmentation zone. The only permitted outbound is to a vendor licensing endpoint (we will provide IP & cert thumbprint).
- HSM: we use an on-prem HSM appliance (Thales) with FIPS 140-2 certificates. We can expose an internal PKCS#11 endpoint but it is isolated; zero internet egress.
- Logging: logs must be forwarded to our central SIEM (on-prem) over syslog/TLS on specific ports; we cannot accept third-party log shippers.
- Data: PHI must not be stored in any third-party S3; encrypted tokenized results may be allowed if stored in our private object store.

Network specifics we will provide in the diagram:
- Allowed CIDR for management: 10.250.0.0/22
- Bastion host only for outbound SSH (jumpbox) — no direct host SSH.
- Outbound allowed ports: 443 (to whitelisted license IP), 853 (DNS over TLS to internal DNS), 514/TLS (syslog).

If Redwood needs to call home for metrics, it must be an opt-in flow and we will require a separate security approval.

Attachments: blueridge-network-sketch.pdf (rough diagram and current firewall ACLs).

We can do Tue 8/24 10:00 PT for the deep-dive — Megan and I will be on the call.

—Daniel Ortiz
Director, Infrastructure & Security
BlueRidge Diagnostics
d.ortiz@blueridge-dx.com | +1 (617) 555-2020

Daniel / team — quick technical notes from our infra side after reviewing your diagram. High level callouts:

- We can support a fully air-gapped deployment model. Two approaches to consider:
  1) On-prem cluster with isolated NAT for licensing checks to a whitelisted IP (preferred for faster time-to-value).
  2) Fully offline bundle & manual license activation (adds ~2–3 weeks and an ops handoff).

- For HSM/KMS: we support PKCS#11 integration. If your Thales box exposes an internal PKCS#11 endpoint reachable from the model hosts and the bastion can broker initial key rotations, we can wire into that. We will need a short window to test key import/export (no keys leave HSM).

- Logging: we will send logs to a local syslog endpoint over TLS (port 514/TCP). We will ensure logs are write-once and can be forwarded only to your SIEM; Redwood will not retain copies by default for the pilot.

- Port requirements (min): 443 outbound to license IP, 514/TCP outbound to SIEM, 22 to bastion (management only), ephemeral 10k–11k range for inter-node RPC (configurable to your firewall).

Action item: we’ll produce a minimal host-level config and a proposed firewall rule set by Tue 8/24 (Priyom owns). Also including a checklist for acceptance tests (performance, data residency verification, and audit log export).

Thanks — happy to discuss specific networking restrictions during the deep-dive.

Ben Carter
